randomized_domain.draw: random.Random(scoring_master_seed) (Python, input generation only; both implementations consume the same committed case file). For each case k = 0..239: file = rng.choice(TARGET_FILES); doc = json.loads(reference file); paths = every node below the root in document order (pre-order, dict insertion order, list index order; a path is a list of keys / indices); p = rng.choice(paths); op = rng.choice(['set', 'set', 'set', 'delete']); value = rng.choice(VALUE_POOL) for set; remanifest = rng.random() < 0.9, forced False when file is MANIFEST.json; pin_override = (file == 'mission/mission_scenario_v2.json') and rng.random() < 0.5 (drawn only for that file). Every loader entry point is evaluated on every case

tolerance_classes.EXACT_BYTES: files / serialized outputs byte-identical (sha256 equal); JSON written with the Python-compatible formatter abep_types::pyjson (shortest round-trip float repr with CPython's tie rule, Python exponent form, indent 1, ensure_ascii False, default separators, insertion key order); formatter verified separately against CPython 3.11.15 (crates/abep-types/tests/pyjson_vectors.rs, seed 202610052)
tolerance_classes.EXACT_VALUE: integers, strings, enums, booleans, statuses, error classes, error messages, schema shape: equal
tolerance_classes.ULP_BOUNDED: NOT_APPLICABLE (no arithmetic beyond float() conversion and one product; both are EXACT_VALUE)

domain_and_error_parity.mapping_rule: every Python exception class raised by the component maps to exactly one Rust ConfigError class name; no Rust path may return a value where Python fails, or fail where Python returns (CLAUDE.md rule 3: no silent fallbacks); every refusal is fail-closed MODEL_ERROR

documented_divergence.statement: a JSON string with a lone UTF-16 surrogate escape: Python holds it in a str, Rust refuses (ValueError)
documented_divergence.disposition: outside the registered domain (no configuration file contains one; the seeded mutations never write one)

documented_divergence.statement: model-set label extraction: Rust tokenizes Python source for top-level `NAME = <str literal(s)>` statements instead of running ast.parse; a module with a syntax error raises SyntaxError in Python but is not necessarily refused by Rust; non-ASCII assignment targets (NFKC-normalized by Python) and \N{...} escapes in a label value are refused by Rust (NotImplementedError); a parenthesized single target `(NAME) = ...` is not recognised
documented_divergence.disposition: outside the registered domain: the reference abep_sim/*.py and the B-15 label module contain none of these; the scored model-set bytes would expose any difference

documented_divergence.statement: build_requirements digit captures (\d+) on clause texts: non-ASCII decimal digits are converted by Python int() but refused by Rust (ValueError)
documented_divergence.disposition: outside the registered domain (registered clause texts are ASCII)

documented_divergence.statement: the builder takes the operating-scenario pin from the Rust loader constant instead of parsing abep_sim/configuration.py with ast
documented_divergence.disposition: INV-03 proves the two pins equal; a changed configuration.py is REFUSED_REFERENCE_CHANGED for this contract anyway

documented_divergence.statement: nesting deeper than 512 levels: Rust RecursionError at its own limit

It is NOT physics validation.
decision_rules.no_retuning: tolerances, observables, inputs, n, seeds and rules are fixed; after NOT_ADMITTED only a code fix plus a new contract version with a fresh scoring_master_seed may follow; the failed report stays; no execution is discarded
decision_rules.disagreement_rule: never rewrite a Python result, golden, fixture, configuration file or frozen dataset to make Rust pass (RM-R11)
decision_rules.observable_scope: observables are restricted to the retained configuration interface; no observable depends on an excluded legacy path (RM-R20)
